claims.statement: Production stacks and the CI runner run as two separate rootless Docker daemons on the same homelab host, publishing into the same host port space, so a prod 0.0.0.0 bind collides with a CI bind on the same port number — and the collision manifests as a crash-loop on the losing side rather than a clean bind error.

The convention reserves host ports 19000–19099 for prod admin/UI publishes; the three prod published ports are Keycloak admin 19099:8080, LangFuse web 19030:3000 and Grafana/otel-lgtm 19002:3000, and every other service in the prod composes is unpublished (reached by Docker DNS on shared networks).

The prod admin/UI publishes bind 0.0.0.0 with a plain HOST:CONTAINER mapping rather than a tailnet-IP-scoped bind, because the rootless daemon starts before tailscaled at boot and a <tailnet-ip>:host:container publish silently fails; tailnet-only exposure is preserved solely by the host's default-deny-inbound firewall posture, which is load-bearing.

scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs classifies a compose file as prod when its basename ends .prod.yaml (under infrastructure-as-code/docker/**) and every other tracked compose file (compose.yaml, compose.ci.yaml, compose.agent-e2e.yaml, stacks/*.compose.yaml) as CI/dev, then fails the scan when a fixed host port appears in both sets.

The collision gate compares host port NUMBERS only: entries with no deterministic fixed host port are skipped (a bare container port, a ${VAR} host field, an unparseable entry), host_ip is ignored, and numeric host-port ranges are expanded.

The collision gate exits 0 when clean or when its selftest passes, 1 on a collision or a broken selftest, and 2 on bad arguments or an unparseable compose file; --selftest plants an overlap on port 19099 and asserts the parser cases so a gate that stopped detecting cannot report green.
The prod↔CI port-collision gate is a required guardrail step: the naming job in .forgejo/workflows/guardrails.yml runs its --selftest and then the scan on every pull request and every push to main.
scripts/preflight.mjs runs the same selftest-then-scan pair for the port-collision gate locally, so a collision is caught before it reaches CI.

The 2026-07-06 prod-auth outage: feature 028 bound the prod Keycloak admin at 0.0.0.0:8099, which overlapped the CI app-e2e Keycloak's 127.0.0.1:8099; a leftover CI stack held the port for 6h, prod Keycloak could not bind on redeploy, and prod auth crash-looped until prod admin ports moved into the reserved range. The failed bind also rolled back keycloak-service's networking, so it came back detached from all networks and could not resolve its own Postgres (UnknownHostException) — which is why keycloak-network is now compose-managed rather than external, created and attached atomically on every `up` so Keycloak can always reach its Postgres even when the shared external networks hit the rootless re-attach race.

Moving or adding a prod published port also requires updating that port's self-referencing URL var, because the collision gate only scans the compose `ports:` key: concretely KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN — set to the :19099 admin URL by the prod-auth stack's `environment` block in infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml and required fail-fast as ${KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN:?} by the keycloak prod compose — and LangFuse's own NEXTAUTH_URL login/callback URL in the observability prod compose. Missing this leaves a working port bind pointing at a stale URL that no port-scan gate can see.

CI tears its stacks down on every run — the app-ci app-e2e job's 'Tear down CI stacks (always)' step runs under if: always() — so a leftover CI stack cannot hold a host port indefinitely and starve a prod redeploy the way the original incident did.

Expo's legacy default dev-server ports 19000/19001/19006 are unused by this project's Expo SDK and the dev container is explicitly told not to forward them, so those numbers are not prod reservations.

The tree-wide topology-scrub gate flags any real tailnet *.ts.net host while allowing sanitized placeholders (any host containing 'tailnet' or 'example'), which is why the reserved range must be discussed as port numbers without a real host paired with a port.
The reserved range 19000–19099 lies below the Linux ephemeral port range (32768+), so a reserved prod published port cannot be transiently claimed by an outbound client connection.

The collision gate discovers candidate compose files with two globs — infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose*.yaml and infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.compose.yaml — and classifies each by basename (a basename ending .prod.yaml is prod, everything else discovered is CI/dev), so a compose file whose name does not begin with 'compose' falls outside the scan.

The prod-auth stack's environment block in infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml no longer passes KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP to the keycloak prod compose (removed 2026-10-12, item #727) and instead carries KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN=http://[[TAILNET_HOST]]:19099. While it was passed, Komodo wrote KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP into .env.prod, which the keycloak prod compose loads with `env_file:`, so it reached the container as a KC_* variable that names no Keycloak option — the admin URL has always used the separate KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN, which is the live var a port move must keep in sync.

TS_ADMIN_IP is now fully retired: it was only ever the bind prefix for the two observability operator UIs, feature 028 made those binds 0.0.0.0 so no compose bind had read it since, and infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml stopped passing it to prod-observability on 2026-10-13 (item #727) — no stack or compose file reads it any more and the operator checklist records the Komodo Variable itself as removed, so a leftover seed could not have failed a deploy and the only cost of one would have been dead config.

Because the collision gate discovers candidate compose files with only two globs (infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose*.yaml and infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.compose.yaml), a CI/dev compose whose basename does not begin with `compose` is never scanned: infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml publishes 0.0.0.0:11434 and is invisible to the gate.

A tree-wide grep for the retired bind-prefix variables KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP and TS_ADMIN_IP surfaces the gates that guarded them rather than live config: scripts/check-komodo-sync.mjs keeps 'KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP=[[TS_ADMIN_IP]]' as a clean-sample fixture and a fake Tailscale address under KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP as a planted-literal fixture, and scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs keeps '${TS_ADMIN_IP}:3030:3000' as a parser case — all deliberately planted selftest inputs, so a grep hit must be checked for fixture/comment status before it is read as a live bind prefix.

Moving a prod admin/UI published port into the reserved range leaves the public auth surface untouched: the public issuer stays the Cloudflare-tunnel hostname that reaches keycloak-service:8080 internally over edge-network, and KC_HOSTNAME_BACKCHANNEL_DYNAMIC keeps the internal discovery document advertising that public issuer, so no client or backend reconfiguration follows — only the tailnet admin-console URL (KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN) moves, which is why a stale admin-console bookmark is the user-visible consequence of the move.

A new or moved prod published port is assigned inside the 19000–19099 range and echoes the number it replaces (8099 → 19099, 3030 → 19030, 3002 → 19002), and the collision gate's failure output prescribes exactly that remedy — move the prod port into the prod-reserved range 19000–19099, or pick a non-overlapping port.

A mechanical guard couples each prod stack's declared inputs to what its composes require: scripts/__tests__/komodo-stack-env.guard.test.mjs parses infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml into one record per [[stack]] (name, run_directory, file_paths, additional_env_files, and the keys of its environment block) and asserts that every `${VAR:?}` in that stack's prod compose is supplied by the environment block or a committed additional_env_files entry — so a required Variable such as KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN or TAILNET_HOST cannot silently disappear from the stack TOML while the compose still demands it. The guard strips comment lines before scanning (a `${VAR:?}` written in a `#` comment is not a requirement), and its second test deletes a live Variable to prove the check is not vacuously green.

That stack↔compose input guard runs in CI as part of the `naming` job's script-unit-test step (`node --test scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs` in .forgejo/workflows/guardrails.yml, added by feature 041 because scripts/__tests__ ran in no workflow) and in scripts/preflight.mjs, so a broken input coupling fails CI rather than surfacing as a failed Komodo deploy — but it only verifies that a required Variable is supplied, not that the port inside its value is still in the reserved range, so a stale `:8099` in KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN passes it.

The reserved admin port also appears in documentation-only artifacts that a port move must update to stay truthful: the committed template infrastructure-as-code/docker/keycloak/.env.prod.example records KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN on the prod-reserved 19099 admin port (noting it was 8099, which collided with the CI Keycloak on the shared host) and keeps the retired KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP only as an explanatory comment, while the runbooks and docs spell out the admin-console URL on 19099 and the LangFuse UI on 19030. No gate reads these, so they drift silently.

The prod-observability environment block in infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml supplies TAILNET_HOST as [[TAILNET_HOST]] (an existing prod-auth Variable reused for LangFuse's NEXTAUTH_URL on :19030, so nothing new to seed) alongside the thirteen LangFuse/Unleash secret Variables, while the compose requires it fail-fast as `${TAILNET_HOST:?}` — so the LangFuse login/callback port lives in the compose as a literal and its host is a stack-TOML value.
